the APT framework provides a useful lens for understanding the role of social interaction for student engagement and learning, while also providing practical guidance for the development of conversational agents supporting peer learning in a classroom environment (Adamson, Dyke et al., 2014) The APT framework has been used to guide the development of a pedagogical agent, called "Socratic Tutor," to support collaborative problem solving activities in a classroom environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that

APT is a framework that is particularly useful for the design of computer supported collaborative activities where students are expected to engage in meaningful discussions, and where the teacher's role is to support the learning process rather than being in full control of the learning environment.
APT is not a set of rigid rules but rather a set of principles that can guide the development of conversational agent interventions to promote productive peer discussions.
